text: The report interprets phylogenetic history as a stronger predictor of gene content than environmental similarity for most bacterial species.
quote: For most bacterial species, phylogenetic history is a stronger predictor of gene content than environmental similarity.
heading: Interpretation

text: The report suggests, rather than directly establishes, that vertical inheritance dominates the gene-content signal.
quote: 1. Vertical inheritance dominates the gene content signal
heading: Interpretation

text: The report proposes that environmental adaptation may affect specific gene subsets rather than whole-genome gene content.
quote: 2. Environmental adaptation may act on specific gene subsets rather than the whole genome
heading: Interpretation

text: AlphaEarth embeddings may miss ecologically relevant environmental variation.
quote: 3. The AlphaEarth embeddings may not fully capture ecologically relevant environmental variation
heading: Interpretation

text: The report cites Garud et al. (2019) and Shapiro et al. (2012) as literature consistent with its phylogeny-dominant interpretation; this is contextual support, not an additional result of this analysis.
quote: - The finding that phylogeny dominates gene content similarity is consistent with work by Garud et al. (2019) and Shapiro et al. (2012) on within-species population structure, which show that clonal ancestry shapes genome-wide variation more than ecological niche.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report relates its weak genome-wide environmental effects to Polz et al. (2013)'s locus-specific horizontal-gene-transfer argument; the proposed gene-subset interpretation remains a hypothesis.
quote: - The weak environmental effects on gene content relate to findings by Polz et al. (2013), who argue that horizontal gene transfer shapes population structure at specific loci rather than genome-wide, consistent with our observation that environment may act on gene subsets rather than the whole genome.
heading: Literature Context

text: AlphaEarth embeddings had only 28.4% genome coverage, limiting the environmental signal available for analysis.
quote: - AlphaEarth embeddings have only 28.4% genome coverage, limiting the environmental signal available for analysis.
heading: Limitations

text: NCBI metadata coordinates are often missing or imprecise, weakening environmental associations.
quote: - Geographic coordinates from NCBI metadata are often missing or imprecise, reducing the quality of environmental associations.
heading: Limitations

text: Partial correlations assume linear relationships between distance matrices and may miss nonlinear ecological effects.
quote: - Partial correlations assume linear relationships between distance matrices, which may not capture nonlinear ecological effects.
heading: Limitations

text: For host-associated organisms, reported latitude and longitude reflect collection sites rather than necessarily reflecting actual microenvironments.
quote: - Host-associated organisms have less meaningful lat/lon data, as the reported coordinates reflect collection site rather than the organism's actual microenvironment.
heading: Limitations
